description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, representing ACC (%), spans from 60 to 80. The Base method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 61% and increases steadily to about 66%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at roughly 65%, rises to a peak of about 73% at a co-occurrence number of 100, then plateaus near 74%. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) starts at around 62% and increases to approximately 67%. The MEMIT method (purple line with star markers) begins at about 65%, rises to a peak of roughly 70% at a co-occurrence number of 100, then increases slightly to about 72%. The IKE method (red line with triangle markers) starts at approximately 65%, rises to about 68% at a co-occurrence number of 100, and then increases to around 69%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) begins at about 72%, rises to a peak of approximately 76% at a co-occurrence number of 100, and then plateaus near 77%.
